findings.title: Credential ownership check fails for team/delegation-owned credentials
findings.body: The authorization check `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })` only matches credentials whose `userId` column equals the current user's id. Credentials belonging to a team (where `userId` is null, e.g. delegation/shared calendar credentials) will never satisfy this condition, so legitimate users managing such credentials will always get an 'access denied' error even though they should be allowed to delete the cache. This makes the feature unusable for any non-personal credential and is inconsistent with how other credential-related handlers in the codebase resolve ownership (typically via a repository helper that also considers team membership/delegation).

findings.title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError loses proper error code
findings.body: `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` produces a generic INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR on the tRPC client instead of a semantically correct code (e.g. NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN via TRPCError). This is inconsistent with tRPC error-handling conventions used elsewhere in the codebase and prevents clients from distinguishing between 'not found' and 'server error' cases, which can also affect logging/alerting noise since legitimate client errors get reported as 500s.

findings.title: deleteCacheMutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query, causing stale cache status in UI
findings.body: Unlike `disconnectMutation`, which has an `onSettled` handler that invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations`, `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop (`onChanged`). If the parent component doesn't pass `onChanged` (it is optional on `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapperProps`), the `cacheUpdatedAt` value shown in the dropdown will not be refreshed after a successful cache deletion, leaving the UI showing a stale 'Cache Status' timestamp even though the cache was actually deleted.

findings.title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: The cache-updated timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {...})`, ignoring the user's configured locale/time format settings used elsewhere in the app. For non-English locales this will render dates in an inconsistent format compared to the rest of the UI.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId updates ALL selected calendars for a credential regardless of which ones were actually refreshed
findings.body: In `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`, after looping over only the `selectedCalendars` passed into the method (which can be a subset, e.g. the 'remainingCalendars' passed from `unwatchCalendar`), the code calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, which updates `updatedAt` for every `SelectedCalendar` row tied to the credential — not just the ones that were actually processed in this call. This produces an inaccurate 'last synced' signal for calendars that weren't touched, and also issues an extra DB write on every cache refresh even when it is a no-op from a data perspective. The PR description itself flags uncertainty about whether this update is even needed.

findings.title: No tests for new deleteCache mutation, cache-status repository method, or CredentialActionsDropdown
findings.body: This PR introduces a new destructive mutation (`deleteCache`), a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), and a new UI component (`CredentialActionsDropdown`) with confirmation-dialog flows, but no unit or integration tests are added for any of them. Given the PR's own review checklist calls out multiple untested behaviors (authorization, cache status mapping, conditional rendering), this is a significant test gap for a feature that deletes user data.

findings.title: updatedAt field combines @default(now()) and @updatedAt; migration uses NOW() instead of Prisma's usual CURRENT_TIMESTAMP default
findings.body: The new `updatedAt DateTime @default(now()) @updatedAt` field combines a static default with the auto-managed `@updatedAt` directive, which is redundant since `@updatedAt` fields are already set to the current time on create. Additionally, the hand-written migration sets the column default as `DEFAULT NOW()` while Prisma's generated migrations for `@default(now())` on Postgres typically emit `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)`. This textual mismatch between the schema-declared default and the actual DB default can cause `prisma migrate dev`/schema-drift detection to flag an unexpected diff in a future migration.

findings.title: Removed `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` type check in findMany
findings.body: The diff removes the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` assertion that previously validated the shape of the args object passed to `prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany`, replacing it with an inline object literal. This is unrelated to the calendar-cache feature and reduces compile-time type safety for this method without any stated reason.
